kf: **Checkpoint inhibitors** (anti-PD-1: nivolumab, pembrolizumab; anti-CTLA-4: ipilimumab) release the brakes on T cells.
Used for advanced and adjuvant melanoma; combination ipilimumab + nivolumab is most effective and most toxic.
**Immune-related adverse events (irAEs)** can affect any organ: skin (commonest), colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, thyroid, pituitary, adrenals, myocarditis.
Any new symptom on immunotherapy: contact the **oncology acute line**; do not wait. Diarrhoea, breathlessness and headache can be life-threatening.
BRAF/MEK inhibitors (dabrafenib + trametinib, encorafenib + binimetinib) for BRAF-mutant disease: fever, photosensitivity, rashes.
myths: **"A rash on immunotherapy means stop treatment"**: most skin irAEs are mild and managed with topical steroids; oncology decides.
patho_lead: Checkpoint inhibitors **remove inhibitory signals** so T cells attack tumour, and sometimes normal tissue.

mech.t: CTLA-4 and PD-1 normally dampen T-cell activation to prevent autoimmunity.
Blocking them reactivates tumour-specific T cells.
mech.cap: Checkpoint inhibitors release the brakes on T cells.

mech.t: Autoreactive T cells cause organ inflammation (irAEs).
mech.cap: Organs affected by immune-related adverse events.

mech.t: Itch, maculopapular rash, lichenoid and psoriasiform eruptions, vitiligo, bullous pemphigoid, rarely SJS/TEN.

comp: Colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathies (often permanent), myocarditis, SJS/TEN.
prog: Durable responses in about half with combination therapy; vitiligo on treatment is associated with better response.
